claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs are governed by formation of a coherent, self-healing mixed-oxide scale.
Al and Cr preferentially segregate to oxidation fronts during high-temperature exposure.
Preferentially segregated Al and Cr form a nanostructured, hierarchical oxide layer.
The proposed mixed-oxide layer reduces oxygen ingress.
The proposed mixed-oxide layer accommodates thermal strain.
The initial material may be a cast or thermomechanically treated Fe-Cr-Al-Ni-Co-type MPEA with a single- or multiphase microstructure.
The controlled intervention is an increase of 2–5 at.% Al or Cr in an otherwise comparable MPEA.
The proposed operating range is 800–1200 °C for 100–500 hours under oxidizing and potentially cyclic thermal conditions.
Increasing Al or Cr produces a coherent, self-adaptive oxide scale enriched in Al or Cr.
Preferential oxidation of Al and Cr at grain boundaries and defect sites rapidly forms a dense, adherent mixed-oxide scale.
The dense mixed-oxide scale slows further oxygen diffusion.
Continued adaptive oxidation heals minor cracks in the oxide scale.
High mixing entropy intrinsically slows diffusion in the alloy.
Slower diffusion minimizes deleterious internal oxidation and preserves the mechanical integrity of the underlying alloy.
Relative to the lower-Al/Cr baseline, the modified alloy will form a thinner, more uniform, and more adherent oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will show lower oxidation weight gain and less scale spallation or cracking.
Improved oxidation behavior will correlate with preserved or enhanced material integrity during long-term high-temperature exposure.

The proposed behavior applies where oxidation kinetics dominate and high mixing entropy retards bulk diffusion, but may fail in reducing atmospheres or when phase transformations or other degradation mechanisms dominate.
The controlled falsification test compares lower-Al/Cr and 2–5 at.% higher-Al/Cr MPEAs during cyclic oxidation in air at 1000 °C for 200 hours.
Failure of the higher-Al/Cr alloy to improve scale thickness, uniformity, adherence, weight gain, or spallation behavior relative to the baseline would reject the hypothesis.
